obligations.summary: An AI system must be classified as high-risk where it is intended to be used as a safety component of (or is itself) a product covered by Annex I Union harmonisation legislation AND that product is required to undergo third-party conformity assessment under that legislation.
AI systems listed in Annex III must be considered high-risk in addition to those qualifying under Article 6(1).
exceptions: An Annex III AI system is not high-risk if it does not pose a significant risk of harm to health, safety, or fundamental rights and fulfils one of the conditions in Article 6(3): performs a narrow procedural task; improves the result of a previously completed human activity; detects decision-making patterns without replacing human assessment; or performs a preparatory task to an Annex III assessment.
The non-high-risk derogation never applies where the AI system performs profiling of natural persons.

obligations.summary: A provider who considers that an Annex III AI system is not high-risk must document that assessment before placing the system on the market or putting it into service, and must make that documentation available to national competent authorities upon request.
A provider who considers that an Annex III AI system is not high-risk is subject to the registration obligation set out in Article 49(2).

The Commission must, after consulting the Board and no later than 2 February 2026, provide guidelines specifying the practical implementation of Article 6 together with a comprehensive list of practical examples of high-risk and non-high-risk AI system use cases.

The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts to amend the conditions in Article 6(3) second subparagraph by adding or modifying conditions where there is concrete and reliable evidence of Annex III AI systems that do not pose a significant risk of harm.

The Commission must adopt delegated acts to amend Article 6(3) second subparagraph by deleting conditions where there is concrete and reliable evidence this is necessary to maintain the level of protection of health, safety, and fundamental rights provided by the Regulation.

Any amendment to the Article 6(3) second subparagraph conditions adopted via delegated acts must not decrease the overall level of protection of health, safety, and fundamental rights and must ensure consistency with delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 7(1) while taking account of market and technological developments.
